```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4)
```

scBrailleR wraps common single-cell plots so that `BrailleR::VI()` can
describe them in text, for screen readers and braille displays. Each
`BR_*()` function returns the usual ggplot unchanged, so you can still
draw it, with the facts needed for a description attached.

This vignette uses `pbmc_small`, the 80-cell example dataset in
SeuratObject. It already has PCA, t-SNE and clusters.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(scBrailleR)
library(Seurat)
data("pbmc_small", package = "SeuratObject")
```

## How many PCs? `BR_ElbowPlot()`

```{r elbow}
p <- BR_ElbowPlot(pbmc_small, ndims = 15)
BrailleR::VI(p)
```

The elbow is the PC furthest from the straight line joining the first
and last points. `Describe = TRUE` adds where 50%, 75% and 90% of the
variance is reached, and a per-PC table:

```{r elbow-long}
BrailleR::VI(p, Describe = TRUE)
```

## Clusters on an embedding: `BR_DimPlot()`

```{r dimplot}
q <- BR_DimPlot(pbmc_small, reduction = "tsne")
BrailleR::VI(q)
```

The output reads in three parts:

- **Per group**: size, centre (the median of each axis) and spread
  (the median absolute deviation of each axis).
- **Isolation**: the distance to the nearest other group's centre,
  divided by the group's own spread. A value well above 1 means a
  separate island; below 1 means it overlaps a neighbour.
- **Two grids** of the plot cut into 4 by 4 squares, with the top row
  being the top of the plot. The density grid counts cells per square.
  The modal grid gives the group most common in each square, which is a
  map of who sits where.

`Describe = TRUE` adds a density grid for each group, on the same
squares, so you can trace one group's shape:

```{r dimplot-long}
BrailleR::VI(q, Describe = TRUE)
```

Colour by any metadata column instead of the active identity:

```{r dimplot-groups}
BrailleR::VI(BR_DimPlot(pbmc_small, reduction = "tsne", group.by = "groups"))
```

## Where is a gene expressed? `BR_FeaturePlot()`

```{r featureplot}
f <- BR_FeaturePlot(pbmc_small, c("CD3E", "LYZ"), reduction = "tsne")
BrailleR::VI(f)
```

For each gene you get how many cells express it, the square with the
highest mean expression and which group is most common there, and the
three groups with the highest mean. The mean-expression grid uses the
same squares as the `BR_DimPlot()` grids, so the two outputs can be
read side by side. `Describe = TRUE` lists every group.

## The plots themselves

The objects are still ordinary plots:

```{r draw, fig.alt = "t-SNE scatter of 80 cells coloured by cluster; see the BR_DimPlot text description above."}
q
```
